_about: Two conversations traced against Girl Effect's Theory of Change: behavioural drivers → intent → service access → behaviour change. Each turn declares the stage it should reach and whether a verified contact should be in the reply.
_why: Knowledge is one driver of eight. A system can answer every question correctly and still never move a girl toward a service, and no retrieval metric would show it. These journeys are the end-to-end check that the product does the thing it exists to do.
_stages: rapport · knowledge · confidence · service_access — from src/observability.STAGE, so the score and the event log agree.

journeys.goal: A girl worried after unprotected sex reaches HIV testing.

turns.message: my friend says you can tell if someone has HIV just by looking at them. is that true?
turns.note: a myth that stops girls testing

turns.message: we didnt use protection last month and i keep thinking about it
turns.note: she names her own risk. Both stages are defensible: it reads as disclosure and as a question about risk, and the reply answers the risk with citations. Marked any rather than forced either way.

turns.message: i think i should get tested but i am scared of what they will say about me
turns.note: intent forming, blocked by anticipated stigma

turns.message: okay tell me what actually happens when you go for an HIV test
turns.note: the conversion turn: she is weighing up going

turns.message: where can i actually go for one?
asante sana aunti, i will text them tomorrow
turns.note: she states an intention to act

journeys.goal: A girl held back by a myth and by family norms reaches family planning.

turns.message: watu wanasema family planning inaharibu mji wa mtoto. is that true?
turns.note: the myth this corpus exists to correct, in her own register

turns.message: my mum would kill me if she found out i was even asking about this
turns.note: the barrier is social, not informational

turns.message: can i even get family planning at my age without my parents agreeing?
turns.note: the measured vocabulary gap: her words against 'informed consent for adolescents'

turns.message: okay so what happens at the clinic when you go for family planning?
where can i get it near me?

turns.note: she states an intention to act, in her own register
